name: Information-highway rhetoric
description: Exploratory road and surfing metaphors used during public introduction of networked communication.
cause_of_death: Documented media decline and contemporaneous irritation with repeated transportation metaphors.

sources.title: What Happened to the Information Superhighway
sources.note: Contemporary Nexis counts show newspaper references dropping from 4562 in 1995 to 842 in 1999.

sources.title: Surfing the Internet: An Introduction Version 2.0.2
sources.note: Preserves Jean Armour Polly's contemporary nontechnical guide and its surfing metaphor.

sources.title: Where does the word cyber come from?
sources.note: Oxford Dictionaries retrospective distinguishes displaced affirmative formations from continuing security terminology.

sources.title: Merging Into Electronic Traffic on Superhighway Is Causing Some Anxiety
sources.note: Contemporary report records irritation with highway puns. Only short lexical fragments retained.

entries.gloss: Browsing represented as adventurous motion rather than routine access.

examples.text: While you are surfing the Web, could you locate the schedule?

entries.rationale: Polly attests the metaphor in 1992; Oxford identifies its dated affirmative register. Annual peak and fade are inferred, not frequency measurements.
